transcript.text: Good morning everyone. We need to plan production for 240 Model X motor drives and 120 Model Y motor drives in the next production window. Before I can sign off on the material allocation and production plan, I need to go through our daily materials review with process engineering, quality, logistics, and product compliance. I'm aware we only have 450 power modules currently released for use, which may not cover the full build. Can I get status updates from each of you on your areas so we can work through this together?

transcript.text: I need to flag something important from my engineering bill-of-materials review. After the latest engineering change, I confirmed that each Model X drive requires exactly 2 power modules and each Model Y drive requires exactly 1 power module. I completed this review but haven't yet entered the revised quantities in the planning system, so the system may not reflect the correct requirements. Based on these figures, the full build of 240 Model X and 120 Model Y drives would require 600 power modules total, which exceeds the 450 currently released.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have an important update from my inspection of the quality-hold area. I found that exactly 150 of the held modules can be recovered after a 6-hour controlled bake followed by insulation testing. I documented this result in a local inspection worksheet, but it hasn't yet been attached to the material record. If we proceed with the bake and testing, those 150 modules could be made available, which combined with the 450 already released would give us 600 total — enough to cover the full build Ravi just described.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have customer shipment confirmations I received by email but haven't yet posted to the shipment board. The Model X order can ship as 180 drives on Friday and 60 drives on Monday, while the Model Y customer requires all 120 drives on Friday. This means we need 180 Model X drives and all 120 Model Y drives completed by Friday — that's 480 power modules (360 for Model X plus 120 for Model Y) needed by Friday, with the remaining 60 Model X drives needed by Monday.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to flag a compliance requirement from my destination review. Every Model Y drive must have serialized power-module traceability and a lot-specific compliance certificate before shipment. I completed the review for the export destination but have not yet added this requirement to the dispatch checklist. This is critical because all 120 Model Y drives are required by Friday, and without the serialized traceability and lot-specific certificates in place, those drives cannot ship even if production is completed.
